Chief Financial Officer — Joe Binz

TAKEAWAYS
Cloud Revenue
-- Reached $1 billion for the first time, representing 26% year-over-year growth.
Annual Run Rate Revenue
-- Surpassed $6 billion.
Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO)
-- Rose by 44% year over year to $3.8 billion and accelerated for three consecutive quarters.
Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
-- Exceeded 120%, with sequential improvement for the third quarter in a row.
Million-Dollar Deals
-- Record number of deals greater than $1 million in annual contract value, nearly doubling year over year.
AI Feature Adoption
-- Robo surpassed 5 million monthly active users, with Teamwork Collection passing 1 million seats sold in less than nine months.
AI Impact on Customer Expansion
-- Companies using AI code generation create 5% more Jira tasks, see 5% higher Jira monthly active users, and expand seats for Jira 5% faster than non-AI users within the software segment.
Seat Expansion Rates
-- Double-digit seat expansion in Teamwork Collection compared to standalone applications.
Service Management Metrics
-- Jira Service Management passed 65,000 customers and claims enterprise growth over 60% year over year; more than two-thirds of service collection customers now use it for non-IT use cases.
Cloud Migration Contribution
-- Migrations contributed a mid- to high-single-digit percentage to cloud revenue growth and are projected to maintain this contribution for the full fiscal year.
Midterm Guidance
-- Management reiterated a 20%+ compounded annual revenue growth target through fiscal 2027 and 25%+ non-GAAP operating margin for fiscal 2027.
Pricing Model Comments
-- Seat-based pricing remains the preferred framework, complemented by select consumption-based models for features like Forge, extra AI credits, and Bitbucket pipelines.
Enterprise Penetration
-- Atlassian Corporation serves more than 350,000 customers, including over 80% of the Fortune 500 and 60% of the Forbes AI 50.
Cross-Sell Momentum
-- Teamwork Collection package, which bundles multiple products and additional AI credits, delivers higher seat expansion and adoption rates, outpacing standalone application conversion.
Buyback and Guidance Update Impact
-- Management noted raised guidance and a significant buyback acceleration, though immediate impact on the share price was addressed as not correlating with operational performance.
Non-Technical Seat Expansion
-- Significant seat growth reported in HR, finance, and other business teams beyond traditional technology user base.
SUMMARY
Atlassian Corporation
(
TEAM

2.99%
)
reported a record-setting $1 billion cloud revenue quarter and achieved annual run rate revenue above $6 billion, citing accelerating demand for AI-powered solutions and multi-year enterprise commitments. The company disclosed that AI adoption is materially increasing usage and seat expansion within core products, and that over 1 million seats were sold for its Teamwork Collection in less than nine months. Management reaffirmed its midterm revenue growth and margin targets, while reiterating proactive pricing discipline and a leading position in enterprise workflow transformation.
CFO Joe Binz emphasized broad-based seat expansion momentum across both technical and non-technical users, with enterprise and SMB segments both contributing to stable growth rates.
CEO Michael Cannon-Brookes cited customer priorities now centering on AI integration, compliance, and unified systems of work, driving a shift to long-term cloud platform deals.
Jira Service Management, now used by more than 65,000 customers and half the Fortune 500, is experiencing its fastest scaleup and strong adoption for non-IT workflows.
Guidance for mid- to high-single-digit cloud migration contributions suggests continued transition from data center deployments, with incentives for cloud upgrades maintained.
The company reported that Teamwork Collection has double-digit higher seat expansion rates than standalone products, strongly correlating with its AI platform and bundled pricing.
Management addressed pricing strategy by highlighting hybrid models and customer preference for predictability, with selective use of consumption-based pricing for advanced workloads.
The company stated that agent-based and AI-enhanced workflows are now operating at scale in both Jira and Service Management, contributing to increased customer stickiness and multi-year commitments.
Atlassian Corporation remains confident in achieving at least 20% compounded annual revenue growth and expanding margins through fiscal 2027, with ongoing risk adjustments in short-term forecasts.
INDUSTRY GLOSSARY
RPO (Remaining Performance Obligations)
: Contracted revenue obliged to be recognized in future periods, representing visibility into booked business not yet delivered.
NRR (Net Revenue Retention)
: A measure of recurring revenue growth from existing customers, accounting for expansions, contractions, and churn.
Teamwork Collection
: Atlassian Corporation’s cloud-based suite bundling multiple collaboration apps and advanced AI credits on a seat-based subscription model.
Jira Service Management (JSM)
: The company’s service desk and workflow automation platform spanning IT, HR, finance, and operations.
Agentic Workflows
: Automated processes executed by software agents or AI within business applications, often replacing or augmenting human input for routine tasks.
MAU (Monthly Active Users)
: The count of distinct users actively engaging with a product or feature within a calendar month.
